invalid_run_rule.note: D8/HIGH-4: if the native-dpdk median @64B is < 600,000 the deployment is bad (not a regression). Mark the run INVALID and exit 2 (infra), do NOT report a gate FAIL (exit 1).

tokio-dpdk.note: Headline tokio-vs-rust gate. The 700k step is judged ONLY here (not per-step - MEDIUM-7).

rust-dpdk.note: D3+D8/HIGH-4: this ONE deployment-normalized gate is BOTH the rust>=native gate AND the sync no-regression gate. Same-run native-dpdk is the denominator, so a slow deployment moves both numbers together and cannot cause a false regression. 1400B is report-only (rust is 81-87% of native when TRex is not line-rate capped - runs #43 #47 #48 #49 #51). The vs-0.3.0 absolute comparison is report-only (see report_only_metrics.vs_0_3_0).

tokio-dpdk-concurrent.note: D2/LOW-3/MEDIUM-1: floor at 64B only (E2 spawn = 232k@512B, 176k@1400B); 512/1400 are report-only. enabled=false => REPORT-ONLY (not gated). PR 4's diff flips enabled:true (PR 4 makes the concurrent path fast). Not keyed on PR_NUMBER.

per_step_tokio_vs_rust.note: D6/HIGH-5/MEDIUM-7: the ONE per-step throughput rule, at 70k/140k/350k ONLY (700k excluded - judged by the headline tokio-dpdk 95%-of-rust gate). tokio-dpdk (fair) rx_pps >= 98% of the SAME-RUN rust-dpdk rx_pps at that step+size (rep 1, a single sample - LOW-9). No '% of offered rate' rule.

idle_cpu.note: Round-5 LOW-3: added by PR 2 as enabled:false (the 0-pps step does not exist yet); PR 5 adds the 0-pps step (task 5.6a) and flips enabled:true. Judged only when the 0-pps step ran (process CPU via pidstat).

dut_latency.note: D5/HIGH-4: DUT p50/p99 are REPORTED, NOT gated. The idle backoff is opt-in and default OFF, so there is no latency hazard in default 0.3.1. There is NO latency gate.

vs_0_3_0.note: D8/HIGH-4/LOW-4: the rust-dpdk-vs-0.3.0-absolute comparison is REPORT-ONLY (a 'vs 0.3.0' column), with a WARN marker below 98% (the brief's sync number). It NEVER gates: CI runs #41 #42 #45 #50 dipped below 97% from deployment variance with same-run native equally low, so gating on the absolute would fail clean runs.
